1	---
2	name: analyze-session
3	description: Analyze a pasted learning-session transcript against a chapter's concept nodes, update per-key-point coverage, recompute progress in the map, and write the next session brief. Use whenever the user finishes a teacher/discussion session and provides or mentions a transcript, asks about coverage or progress, or wants the next session prepared, even if they only say "session done".
4	---
5	
6	# Analyze Session
7	
8	Compares a session transcript to the chapter's nodes, updates coverage, and prepares the next brief. Run from the vault root.
9	
10	## Find the inputs
11	
12	- Chapter folder: the one the user names; if several exist and it's unclear, ask.
13	- Transcript: the file the user names, otherwise the newest file in `<Chapter>/sessions/` that has no `## Analysis` heading. If none, ask the user to paste the transcript into `sessions/Session-N.md`.
14	
15	Read `_map.md`, every file in `nodes/`, and the transcript.
16	
17	## Marking rules (per key point)
18	
19	Only use evidence from this transcript. Never invent coverage.
20	
21	- `[x]` **covered**: the idea was explained with its reason or mechanism, AND the learner engaged with it (asked about it, restated it, reasoned about it, or the exchange went beyond the teacher just stating it).
22	- `[/]` **mentioned**: the teacher stated or named it but the learner moved on without engaging, or it was only named without its mechanism.
23	- `[ ]` untouched.
24	- If the learner engaged but got it wrong or stayed confused, mark `[/]`, not `[x]`.
25	- Never downgrade a key point that is already `[x]`. If unsure, leave it unchanged.
26	- Do not edit key point text, add key points, or touch `source.pdf`. Only change the checkbox markers.
27	
28	Transcript quirks: it comes from a voice chat. Speaker labels may be missing (infer from context), and technical terms may be misheard (match them to the nearest term in the nodes). Lines starting with "Outside the chapter:" are tangents, not coverage.
29	
30	## Shaky items
31	
32	When the learner said something wrong, was corrected by the teacher, or voiced confusion that wasn't resolved, add a line under that node's `## Notes`:
33	`- Session N: shaky - <one-line description>`
34	Only when there is clear evidence.
35	
36	## Recompute
37	
38	- Node `coverage` (frontmatter) = round(100 x `[x]` / total key points).
39	- Group and overall coverage = `[x]` over all key points beneath them (not an average of percentages).
40	- Update `_map.md` with the new numbers.
41	
42	## Log the session
43	
44	Append to the transcript file:
45	
46	```
47	## Analysis
48	- Covered this session: <Concept>: n key points, ...
49	- Mentioned only: <Concept>, ...
50	- Shaky: ...
51	- Tangents (outside the chapter): ...
52	```
53	
54	## Write the next brief
55	
56	Overwrite `_brief.md`. Session number = previous + 1. Mode is `directed`.
57	
58	```
59	# Session Brief - <Chapter> - Session N
60	Mode: directed
61	Progress: X% covered
62	
63	## Plan (in order)
64	1. Concept title - open key points:
65	   - key point text (p.N)
66	   Revisit: <mentioned-only or shaky items, if any>
67	2. ...
68	
69	## Already covered - do not re-seed
70	- Concept, Concept
71	
72	## Notes
73	- Threads the learner cared about (what they kept asking about)
74	- Tangents worth queueing
75	```
76	
77	Plan rules: at most 4 concepts. Order: first the concepts with `[/]` or shaky items (revisit), then uncovered concepts whose `depends_on` are mostly covered. If none qualify, take the next uncovered concepts in source order. List only open key points (`[ ]` and `[/]`).
78	
79	If everything is `[x]`, say so and write a brief with `Mode: done` and no plan.
80	
81	## Report in chat (short)
82	
83	- Overall coverage: before -> after
84	- What moved (concepts that gained key points)
85	- Shaky items, if any
86	- What the next session targets
87	
88	State plainly that coverage measures what was explored, not mastery; the shaky flags are the only understanding signal for now.
```

1	---
2	name: ingest-chapter
3	description: Turn a chapter PDF (lecture slides or textbook chapter) into an Obsidian concept map: one node file per concept with a key-point checklist, a hierarchy map, and a first session brief. Use whenever the user wants to set up, ingest, map, or decompose a new chapter for interrogation-style learning, or hands over a chapter PDF to build the vault from, even if they don't say "ingest".
4	---
5	
6	# Ingest Chapter
7	
8	Builds the study vault for one chapter. Run from the vault root. The PDF is the only source of truth: never add content from outside it.
9	
10	Input: a PDF path (ask if missing) and a chapter name (default: from the PDF title or filename).
11	
12	## Output layout
13	
14	```
15	<Chapter>/
16	  source.pdf
17	  _map.md
18	  _brief.md
19	  nodes/<Node Title>.md
20	  sessions/
21	```
22	
23	## Steps
24	
25	1. **Read the PDF fully.** Copy it to `<Chapter>/source.pdf`. Extract text per page (`pdftotext -layout` if available, otherwise read the PDF directly). If slides are mostly diagrams or images, look at the pages as images. Track PDF page numbers for everything.
26	
27	2. **Decompose by function, not by slide order.** A node is a group of information that serves the same problem, mechanism, process, relationship, design choice, or tradeoff. Do not make one node per slide. A concept usually spans 1-4 pages and one page can feed several concepts.
28	   - Two levels only: **Groups** (broad themes) and **Concepts** (leaves).
29	   - Size guide: roughly 1 concept per 1-3 pages, so a 40-slide chapter lands around 15-25 concepts.
30	
31	3. **Write key points for each concept.** 3-6 atomic ideas the learner should walk away with, one sentence each, each with a page reference. Favor the why, how, and tradeoff over bare definitions. Every key point must be traceable to the source.
32	
33	4. **Set dependencies.** For each concept, list the concepts that should be understood first (`depends_on`).
34	
35	5. **Coverage check.** Every page with substantive content must feed at least one node. List any that don't under "Unmapped pages" in `_map.md`.
36	
37	6. **Write the files** in the formats below. Filenames are the node titles; avoid `/ : ? * " < > |` in titles.
38	
39	7. **Show the hierarchy in chat** (indented list of groups and concepts) and ask the user to approve or adjust it. This is the only question you ask. Apply any changes, then finish.
40	
41	## Concept node format
42	
43	```
44	---
45	type: concept
46	parent: "[[Group Title]]"
47	depends_on: ["[[Other Concept]]"]
48	pages: [12, 13]
49	coverage: 0
50	---
51	# Concept Title
52	**Problem:** one line
53	**Mechanism:** one to three lines
54	**Tradeoffs / consequences:** one line, only if the source says
55	
56	## Key points
57	- [ ] Sentence stating the idea. (p.12)
58	- [ ] Sentence stating the idea. (p.13)
59	
60	## Notes
61	```
62	
63	## Group node format
64	
65	```
66	---
67	type: group
68	coverage: 0
69	---
70	# Group Title
71	One-line theme.
72	```
73	
74	## _map.md format
75	
76	```
77	# <Chapter> - Map
78	Overall coverage: 0%
79	
80	## <Group Title> - 0%
81	- [[Concept A]] - 0%
82	- [[Concept B]] - 0%
83	
84	## Unmapped pages
85	- none
86	```
87	
88	Coverage is the share of key points marked `[x]`, counted across all key points (not an average of averages).
89	
90	## _brief.md format (first session)
91	
92	```
93	# Session Brief - <Chapter> - Session 1
94	Mode: free-run
95	Progress: 0% covered
96	
97	## Opening seed
98	2-3 sentences, in your own words, stating the chapter's core problem and what the system is trying to achieve. Not a question.
99	
100	## Plan (in order)
101	1. Concept title - open key points:
102	   - key point text (p.N)
103	2. ...
104	
105	## Already covered - do not re-seed
106	- none
107	
108	## Notes
109	- First session is a free run: the learner leads, the plan is only a reference.
110	```
111	
112	Order the plan by dependencies (prerequisites first).
113	
114	## Finish
115	
116	Tell the user in two lines: how many groups and concepts were created, and to open the vault in Obsidian (graph view works because of the links).
```

# Interrupt Processing
**Problem:** Return to the interrupted program exactly where it left off.
**Mechanism:** Hardware acknowledges the interrupt, pushes PSW and PC onto the control stack, and loads a new PC; software saves the rest of the process state, handles the interrupt, then restores state and the old PSW and PC.

## Key points
- [ ] Hardware steps: the device issues an interrupt, the processor finishes the current instruction, signals acknowledgment, pushes PSW and PC onto the control stack, and loads a new PC value based on the interrupt. (p.28)
- [ ] Software steps: save the remainder of the process state information, process the interrupt, restore process state information, then restore the old PSW and PC. (p.28)
- [ ] The return address (N+1) goes on the control stack while the PC is loaded with the start of the interrupt service routine; on return it is restored so the user program resumes at N+1. (p.29)
- [ ] The general registers and stack pointer are part of the state saved and restored around the handler. (p.29)
